items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: But if there's anyone I am grateful to, it's my Uncle Jim for, I guess, spurring me on like that to play.

ctx.x:
or what it meant to a grown-up, much less a kid.
So when he said this, I guess my ears just perked up. I felt like it was no problem to me, because I liked to fool with this thing anyway. So I sat down, and as I said, by this time it was around 7 o'clock, I guess. And by the time I went to bed that night, at 10:30 or 11 o'clock, I was playing a piece with two fingers, two-part harmony... But I had learned this little piece that we used to sing in Sunday School and at school, too, a piece called "Lift Every Voice…

I didn't see my uncle for another three or four weeks. And the fact is that I never did get the five dollars. But if there's anyone I am grateful to, it's my Uncle Jim for, I guess, spurring me on like that to play. I don't think that he would have had to do that, but it did help a little bit. And of course, I have a lot of other people to thank for it.
But from that day on, it was every day at the piano. School started about two-three weeks from there. And I remember when I went to school I could hardly wait to get back
